create.name: Ce0.95Mn0.05O2
create.synthesis_para: CeO2 and Mn, Cu and Ag doped CeO2 were prepared via tartaric acid assisted solution combustion method. The preparations were carried out by dissolving the calculated amount of Ammonium cerium nitrate (Ce(NH4)2(NO3)6) and respected metal nitrate salts (AgNO3, Mn(NO3)2·4H2O and Cu(NO3)2·3H2O) in double distilled water. Weighed amount of tartaric acid was added under constant stirring and heating to above metal nitrate mixture, which further kept at 80 °C in an electric oven. The formed gel was than heated to 200 °C for 2 h and then calcined at 500 °C for 4 h to get respective metal oxide.

create.name: Ce80Co20
create.synthesis_para: Nanocomposite Ce80Co20−xFexO2 (x = 0, 5, 10, 15, 20) catalysts were synthesized using the CTAB-assisted co-precipitation method. In detail, Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and Co(NO3)3·6H2O were dissolved in deionized water in molar ratios of Ce/Co/Fe = (80:20:0, 80:15:5, 80:10:10, 80:5:15, 80:0:20). Then, a certain amount of CTAB was added into the aforementioned salt solution (with a molar ratio of CTAB to metal ions = 1.5:1) and mixed together under stirring conditions to obtain a clear homogeneous precursor solution. To maintain the pH value of the solution at approximately 11, the mixture solution was precipitated by drop-wise addition of a 1 M NaOH solution under vigorous stirring. Afterward, the obtained slurry was aged for 3 h at 80 °C in the mother liquor. The resulting light-colored slurry was precipitated, filtered and washed several times with sufficient deionized water and alcohol until it was completely free from sodium ions and surfactant. Finally, the obtained precipitate was oven dried for 12 h at 110 °C and calcined in the air for 6 h at 550 °C at a heating rate of 2 °C/min. According to the molar ratios, the prepared samples are denoted as Ce80Co20, Ce80Co15Fe5, Ce80Co10Fe10, Ce80Co5Fe15 and Ce80Fe20, respectively.

create.name: CoCeOx-0.5-NP
create.synthesis_para: The CoCeOx materials were synthesized through the hard-templating method. A certain amount of Co(NO3)2·6H2O and Ce(NO3)3·6H2O (mole ratio of Co/Ce = 0.5, 1, and 2) were dissolved in 20.0 mL mixed solution of methanol and ethylene glycol (volumetric ratio = 3:1). Besides, a certain amount of chelating agent (citric acid) was added and stirred for 3 h until a transparent mixed solution was obtained. Then, 5.0 g of PMMA was impregnated in the hybrid solution for 6 h and removed the excess solution by vacuum filtration. The obtained solids were dried at 30 °C for 48 h, then heated at 300 °C for 2 h in pure N2. Finally, the solids were calcinated at 500 °C for 3 h in the air. The obtained samples with different Co/Ce were denoted as CoCeOx-0.5-NP, CoCeOx-1-NP, and CoCeOx-2-NP. For comparison, Co3O4-NP and CeO2-NP were also synthesized in the same method as above.

create.name: Fe0.67Ce0.5O2
create.synthesis_para: The solid solutions were synthesized by hydrothermal method. In a typical process, 8 mL of NaOH (6 M) aqueous solution was dropwise added into 88 mL of cerium nitrate (Ce(NO3)3⋅6 H2O) and the aqueous solution of second metal (0.1 M, Fe(NO3)3⋅9 H2O, Ni(NO3)2⋅6 H2O, Mn(NO3)2⋅6 H2O and Ti(C4H9O)4) under vigious stirring. The solution was then transferred into a Teflon lined Autoclave to proceed the hydrothermal treatment for 48 h at 90 °C. After that, the suspension was cooled down to room temperature and filtered. The solid was washed with deionized water and ethanol for several times, dried overnight at 60 °C and finally calcined at 600 °C for 4 h in air flow to get the catalysts which were named as Mn+(4–4x)/nCexO2 (here x = 0.5 for Fe, Mn and Ti, x = 0.975 for Ni).

create.name: Ce-Mn
create.synthesis_para: The loofah sponges were cleaned with distilled water and cut into pieces approximately 2 mm thick. They were then treated in a 30% NaOH solution at 98 °C for 1 h. After washing alternately with anhydrous ethanol and distilled water, the treated loofah sponges were immersed in a 0.2 M mixed solution of water and ethanol (1:1 volume ratio) containing CeO2 and metal salts (M/Ce = 0.4, where M = Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, La) under ultrasonic vibration. The impregnated sponges were subsequently washed with anhydrous ethanol to remove excess salts and dried at 120 °C for 1 h under vacuum. Finally, the samples were placed in a quartz tube furnace and calcined at 600 °C in air for 1 h at a heating rate of 5 °C/min. The resulting catalysts were denoted as Ce-Mn, Ce-Fe, Ce-Co, Ce-Ni, Ce-Cu, and Ce-La, respectively.

create.name: Ce0.8Bi0.2O2
create.synthesis_para: Nanosized mixed oxides of cerium and bismuth (CeO2–Bi2O3) were synthesised using a coprecipitation method using metal precursor salts, Aldrich AR grade cerium(iii) nitrate hexahydrate and bismuth(iii) nitrate pentahydrate. Required quantities of the metal nitrate salts with respect to the required molar ratios were dissolved in deionized water and an aqueous ammonia solution (25% w/v) was added dropwise at room temperature under continuous stirring to obtain pH ≈ 8.5. Once the pH reached 8.5 the addition of ammonia solution was stopped and the solution was stirred for 24 h.35 The obtained solution was aged for 3 days and filtered to separate the precipitates. To remove the remaining anion impurities, the precipitate was washed with distilled water and dried in an oven at 120 °C overnight. The resulting solid compounds were ground into fine powders which were further calcined at 500 °C for 5 h with a temperature at 5 °C min−1 under an air atmosphere. Similarly, pure forms of CeO2 and Bi2O3 were also prepared with the abovementioned method.

create.name: CeO2-Sm2O3
create.synthesis_para: The CeO2-Sm2O3 and CeO2-La2O3 solid solutions with a reference CeO2 were synthesized using a precipitation method from ultra-high dilute aqueous solutions. The employed metal precursors are Ce(NO3)3·6H2O (Aldrich, AR grade), Sm(NO3)3·6H2O [Aldrich, AR grade] and La(NO3)3·6H2O (Aldrich, AR grade). Dilute aqueous ammonia solution was used as the precipitating agent. In brief, to synthesize the 40% Sm doped CeO2, the requisite quantities of metal precursors were dissolved in double distilled water separately, and mixed together under vigorous stirring conditions. The mixed solution was precipitated by drop-wise addition of aqueous ammonia solution over a period until the pH of the solution reached ~8.5. The resulting pale yellow colored slurry was decanted, filtered off, and washed several times with double distilled water. The obtained precipitate was oven-dried at 373 K for 12 h and finally calcined at 773 K for 5 h at a heating rate of 5 K/min in air atmosphere
